Inglewood, California
  March 19, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 19, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 15, 2019, in the amount of $97,052.11, and dated March 15, 2019, in the amount
  of $3,862,706.58 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney were presented
  recommending denial of the following claims:
  a) Emily Chaidez for alleged personal injury on August 27, 2018.
  b) Sharon Gallego for alleged property damage on January 4, 2019.
  c) Curtis Gardenshire for alleged property damage on August 2, 2018.
  d) Christopher Jefferson for alleged property damage on January 5, 2019.
  e) Carol Matthews for receipt of incomplete records on December 26, 2018.
  f) Montre Smith for alleged property damage on February 12, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  and carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  1
 March 19, 2019

 101  AGREEMENT NO. 19-148(A) APPROVED – MEDINA MASONRY. Staff report
  dated March 19, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with
  Medina Masonry to install bollards throughout Parking Garage #2 located at 115 South
  Locust Street.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member Dotson that the City Council/Successor
  Agency does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-148(A) in the amount of $18,420;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor/Chairman to execute Agreement No. 19-148(A). The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin
  and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Member Franklin, and seconded by Successor
  Agency Member Morales that the Successor Agency does hereby approve the use of tax
  exempt bond funds for the work to be performed by Medina Masonry (as required by the
  Agreement) in a total contract amount of $18,420. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Chairman
  Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Morris Griffin, (Big Money Griff), asked the City Council to consider his proposal asking
  local hardware stores to get rid of the 9% sales tax to Inglewood home owners to help
  offset the cost to rehabilitate their property. He stated by doing this, landlords will not
  have to raise their rents.

  Willie Agee stated that he owned property here in Inglewood but got rid of it due to the
  hassle.

  Erick Holly, Executive Vice President of the Chamber of Commerce invited everyone to
  attend the State of the City address on April 18, 2019, at the Hyatt LAX. He stated
  tickets are available by calling 310-677-1121.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Mark Campbell, 31-year Inglewood Police Officer, long-time
  resident John Warren Lemon, and District 3 resident Hermila Luna, at the hour of 2:26
  p.m.

  Approved this 2nd day of April, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
